A rerun re-executes the container against the
same submitted files, so submitted_at does not
change on rerun. That makes it a reliable
marker of exactly which submission was graded.

Why a stored column rather than a query over
test_outcome: the rule is not always
"any test failed". It may be a partial-credit
threshold, a target-specific condition in the
instructor's autograder, or a manual decision.
Storing the decision and its reason makes the
marking auditable, which matters because every
feedback_mode is per target, so one submission
can have IMMEDIATE targets graded during the
submission run and NIGHTLY targets left for a
How many times results.json is written depends

all IMMEDIATE -> written once, guard set,
any NIGHTLY -> written twice, once on the
submission run and once on the rerun

What is specific to mixed mode is partial
feedback that reads as complete.** The first
IMMEDIATE targets and silence on the NIGHTLY
ones. A student's reasonable inference is that
the silent targets were fine, which is exactly
backwards if they failed and are queued.
All-NIGHTLY does not have this problem:
zero feedback reads as "not graded yet".
Mitigation, cheap and worth doing: the
packager emits a placeholder for every task
that is NEEDED but not DONE, saying feedback
is being generated and will appear by the next
morning. See the packager note in 07.
One more consequence to accept: an IMMEDIATE
target whose grading failed is also still
NEEDED, so it is retried on the nightly run
and its feedback arrives the next morning
A registered target with no outcome is an
error.** If the instructor's suite never calls
record_outcome for a target registered on this
assignment, the AI phase fails the autograder
run with a diagnostic naming the missing
Rationale: the alternative is a silent skip,
and a silently skipped target produces no
feedback with no explanation, which is the
failure mode hardest to debug from the
One thing to weigh: on Gradescope this error
is visible to the student, not just the
instructor, and it blocks their score. That is
the correct trade for a misconfigured
assignment that needs fixing immediately, but
the message should say plainly that the
assignment is misconfigured and the student
OQ-2 confidence (FR-28) has a column but no
OQ-4 resubmissions. As drawn every attempt is
submission_file holds student source code and
identifiers, and in immediate mode that code
is sent to a third-party LLM within seconds of
submission. Privacy, retention and consent are
out of scope in the SRS, which is fine for a
design doc and not for a live course. Raise
with Pitt before real submissions land here.
